submissions.findingTextShort: A 16-RCT meta-analysis found no cognitive benefit from B12/B-complex supplementation in people without overt B12 deficiency or advanced neurologic disease.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A systematic review, meta-analysis, and meta-regression of 16 randomized controlled trials involving 6,276 participants without advanced neurological disease or overt vitamin B12 deficiency found no evidence that vitamin B12 alone or B-vitamin combinations improved cognitive subdomains. The synthesis also did not support a robust general enhancement effect on depressive symptoms or idiopathic fatigue. These findings constrain use of B12 as a cognition or energy enhancer in nondeficient populations.
submissions.populationContext: Participants without overt B12 deficiency or advanced neurologic disease across randomized trials.
submissions.usageContext: Vitamin B12 alone or in B-vitamin combinations; formulation and co-nutrients varied.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Null enhancement evidence does not negate treatment of true deficiency.

submissions.findingTextShort: B12 corrects biochemical deficiency, while cognitive improvement was confined to people with pre-existing deficiency rather than B12-replete users.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A review of vitamin B12 and cognitive impairment found that high-dose oral or parenteral B12 corrected biochemical deficiency and that cognitive improvement was observed in patients with pre-existing B12 deficiency, while B12 therapy did not improve cognition in patients without pre-existing deficiency. Deficiency correction is therefore distinct from nootropic enhancement.
submissions.populationContext: People with low B12 or deficiency and comparison populations without established deficiency.
submissions.usageContext: Oral or parenteral vitamin B12 treatment; route and form depend on clinical context.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Association between low B12 and neurodegenerative disease is not itself proof of treatment efficacy outside deficiency.

submissions.findingTextShort: A neurologic B12-deficiency synthesis found short-course signals in susceptible populations but inconsistent longer-term cognitive improvement.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A systematic review and meta-analysis of neurological implications of vitamin B12 deficiency reported short-term neurological or cognitive improvement in some susceptible populations after correction, while longer-term supplementation findings were inconsistent and many controlled trials did not show sustained cognitive improvement. This reinforces the boundary between deficiency treatment and durable enhancement claims.
submissions.populationContext: B12-deficient or susceptible populations across heterogeneous studies.
submissions.usageContext: Vitamin B12 correction or supplementation in deficiency-related neurologic contexts.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Heterogeneous populations and durations constrain broad conclusions.

submissions.findingTextShort: A 2026 Cochrane review found B12 supplementation reduced deficiency but may have little to no effect on cognition, growth, development, or anemia in children.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A 2026 Cochrane review of 16 trials in children found that vitamin B12 supplementation reduced B12 deficiency and improved B12 concentrations, while evidence suggested little to no effect on cognitive function, growth, development, or anemia across several comparisons. Pediatric nutritional and developmental evidence must remain separate from adult enhancement claims.
submissions.populationContext: Children younger than 12 years across nutritional and deficiency-risk contexts.
submissions.usageContext: Oral B12 alone or with micronutrients; doses, durations, and baseline status varied.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Certainty ranged from high to very low by outcome; few studies reported several clinical outcomes or adverse effects.

submissions.findingTextShort: The live Cobalamin profile states deficiency-treatment outcomes with zero receipts, generic form-only dosage text, and no explicit form-owner boundary.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: The current NOINDEX Cobalamin profile states that B12 corrects deficiency and prevents deficiency-related anemia and neuropathy while exposing sourceCount zero and no claim map. Its dosage fields contain only `capsule or softgel`, which is a product form rather than a regimen. Generic cobalamin also coexists with separate form-specific owners such as methylcobalamin, so evidence and dosing must not be silently shared across forms without an explicit ontology rule.
submissions.usageContext: Repository evidence-receipt, dosage-template, and entity-form boundary finding.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: This record does not propose a consumer dose or absorb the separate methylcobalamin workpack. Keep NOINDEX until governed reconciliation.
